author: Widogeist
body:
1. You should be able to access pretty much everything while playing at home, although it will be a little more difficult (and definitely slower).  Your biggest hurdle would probably be finding dungeons, however, there are things called "wayvessels" which let you teleport to a party member's location (wherever they have their wayvessel set); you can likely find people with some dungeons that you can use.

2. There is no energy bar or gameplay cap like other games have.  The only thing stopping you from playing is yourself.  There are some timers on certain things however: Kingdom raids have a 1 hour lockout (if you die, you have to wait 1 hour to fight the specific raid again), wayvessels have a 1 hour cooldown, dungeons have different cooldown timers depending on the type/difficulty you do (normal, boss, hardmode, endless, etc), and if you die to a monster/boss you have to wait 5 minutes to re-engage it.  There are probably others I'm forgetting, but those are the main ones.

3. Level 250 is the current cap; there is no ascension level cap, although ascension levels get progressively more expensive & harder to achieve the higher you get.

4. The only type of cheating in Orna that I'm aware of is GPS spoofing, which mostly comes into play with territory control. Odie and the rest of the team are pretty quick to respond to reports of cheating though, so if you suspect a possible spoofer, toss an email to help@playorna.com and they will investigate.  I've never heard of reports about gold/material/orns cheating, but who knows.

5. The only real restrictions on multiplayer/co-op play are cooldowns on your wayvessel, cooldown timers on dungeons, etc. Your friend could pop over to your wayvessel and you guys could sit there and kill monster/boss spawns for hours if you wish.  With PVP there are two main forms: PvP vs. AI/computer, and Live PvP where you face other players in real time. PvP vs. AI (called "sparring" in-game) is always accessible and matches are instantaneous. Live PvP is dependent on if there are any other players trying to do live pvp too at that specific time.  If no one else is searching for a match, then you won't match anyone (live pvp isn't very popular).

6. Every 25 levels you reach a new tier.  This means your next tier class will become available to unlock (providing you have enough orns and your prerequisite classes are bought), and world monster spawns will scale up to the next tier.  Levels 1-24 is T1, 25-49 is T2, 50-74 is T3, 75-99 is T4, etc.  You can still occasionally get lower tier monsters/bosses to spawn, but the majority of spawns will be equal or around your current tier.  There are also consumable items in the game which can force monsters to spawn closer to your tier, so you don't get lower level enemies (called affinity candles).

7. If you dedicate enough time to the game, yes in theory you can get every item, pet, etc.  There are monthly exclusive raids/monsters/pets so you would have to wait for them to come around again, but you should be able to collect everything.  Anything that comes to alpha/beta is eventually released to the public version.

author: Essurio
body:
1) A few things, most of which are not especially important. But in the next big update there will be important content that can only be accessed by travelling.
2) No. Yes.
3) 250 is the max level and as far as I know there is no cap to ascensions.
4) Depending on where you live. I have 1 guy who I am 99.99% sure is a cheater (a high level one too), but there are people who I know, that don't have any cheaters (or they are just really good at hiding it).
5) You can always pvp, but the real time pvp is not too popular. There are no restrictions like that, only arena tokens for pvp.
6) Enemies don't scale, but you have to play a lot (especially if you only play from home) to get to max level and high ascensions.
7) Probably not, there are exclusive things for each month, however those come back, so you just have to be patient. The only things you cannot get are removed items and really exclusive things. (Like the fishing competition and other exclusive sprites)
